data.passage:
Ginny filled out the long application for a job with Judge Phillips. Judge Phillips was a magistrate judge whose job was to handle each criminal or civil case with integrity. Ginny felt that working for this judge would give her the chance to do some important work.

Ginny knew there were many applications landing on Judge Phillips’ desk. She reflected on how she might get hers to the top of the pile. Then, it hit her. She had half a mind to introduce herself to the judge to get an edge in the process.

Ginny found out that a reception was to be held at the city hall and the judge would be attending. Ginny made plans to go and make a face-to-face introduction. She would then be able to mention to the judge that she was an applicant for the open position.

Although she did not wish to be an imposition on the judge, Ginny had the strong intention of bumping into her at the reception. At last, Ginny saw the judge standing alone. This was her one chance. Ginny went up to the judge and extended her hand. The judge was friendly and impressed with Ginny’s motivation.

The next day, Ginny got a call from the judge whom she had met in person the evening before. The judge had been struck by Ginny’s passion for the constitution. She made the suggestion that Ginny set up a time to connect with her once again. Things were looking good for Ginny’s application!

questions.question: What job did Ginny apply for?
What kind of judge was Judge Phillips?
Why did Ginny want to work for Judge Phillips?
What problem did Ginny see with the applications on the judge’s desk?
What plan did Ginny make after learning about the reception?
What did Ginny do when she saw the judge standing alone?
How did the judge respond to Ginny?
Why did the judge contact Ginny the next day?
What can you infer about Ginny’s motivation from her actions?
Do you think Ginny’s decision to attend the reception helped her application? Use details from the passage.
